أُسْكُوبٌ : see سَكْبٌ, in three places. ―
-b2- Also Lightning extending towards the earth. (K.) So in the saying of Zuheyr El-Mázinee, “بَرْقٌ يُضِىْءُ أَمَامَ البَيْتِ أُسْكُوبُ
” [Lightning shining, or shining brightly, before the tent, or house, extending towards the earth]; as though it were pouring forth rain. (TA.) ―
-b3- And A row of palm-trees; (IAar, K;) as also أُسْلُوبٌ: if of other than palm-trees, it is termed أُنْبُوبٌ, and مِدَادٌ. (IAar, TA.) ＝
-A2- Also i. q. إِسْكَافٌ [A maker of shoes or boots, or a sewer of leather, &c.]; like ↓ إِسْكَابٌ : or a blacksmith. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
